exercise.name: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl
aliases: Single-leg stability ball curl with diagonal kick
Swiss ball one-leg hamstring curl and kick

reference.title: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the ball curls in and the leg kicks, inhale as both return.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s in, 0.5 s hold, 1.8 s out

prescription.progression: Slower return, or arms across the chest

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms on the floor, left heel on the ball, right leg up in line, hips lifted.
Breathe out, curl the ball in with the left heel and kick the straight right leg up and across.
Breathe in, roll the ball back out and bring the right leg back in line.
Keep the hips off the floor; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the hips as the ball rolls in
mistakes.fix: Drive the hips up as the heel comes in.
Press the heel straight down through the middle of the ball.
Roll out over about 2 s with the hips up.

kinematics.norm: From near straight to about 80-100 degrees (clinical opinion); Swiss ball curls load the hamstrings (Escamilla 2016)
Straight leg to about 60-80 degrees of hip flexion, across the midline (clinical opinion)
Rolls toward the glutes under the heel (standard technique)

sources.title: GymVisual #13796, Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl, video (movement reference)
Escamilla, Lewis, Pecson, Imamura and Andrews 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379; PMC4922527)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Use a ball rated for exercise, inflated firm, on a non-slip mat.
Hamstring cramp: stop and use both legs.
modify: Both heels on the ball (two-leg curl).
regressions: Lying hip lift on a stability ball.
progressions: Pause with the ball curled in.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Curl the ball in on one leg while holding the hips up (Escamilla 2016, Swiss ball curls).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the straight right leg into the diagonal kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Steadies the trunk on one leg and the ball (Escamilla 2016).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the twist of the diagonal kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the twist of the diagonal kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Draw the kicking leg across (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen as the straight leg kicks up (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Hips up, one heel on the ball

guides.label: Ball leg curls to about 90 degrees
